content.content:
===== UlRemedyForever
# UlRemedyForever

A lightweight quality-of-life collection for **World of Warcraft: Forever**. A dozen small utilities in one addon, each individually toggleable with a slash command. Settings persist between sessions.

A separate addon from [UlRemedy](https://github.com/Knitresletta/UlRemedy) (retail). Only the features that make sense in Forever are included.

> **Status:** tested in-game on the Forever beta client (build 1.60.1).

## Price sharing: what leaves your machine

Since 1.10.0 the addon **shares auction prices with other UlRemedyForever users on your realm**, and this is **on by default**. Read this before you decide to keep it.

- **How:** addons have no network access. The only way two addons can talk is addon messages over the game's chat system. The addon joins a chat channel named `UlRemedyAH` (kept out of your chat windows, but it takes a channel number) and sends addon messages there. Nobody sees them as text.
- **What is sent:** item ID, lowest buyout per unit and the age of that price, for the prices *this character saw itself* at the auction house in the last 24 hours, plus a short hello on joining that says how fresh your newest price is. The chat system attaches your character name to every message, as it does to all chat.
- **What is never sent:** gold, bag or bank contents, other characters, and prices you received from others (nothing is relayed, so nothing echoes around the channel).
- **When:** after a full scan (unless someone else's broadcast came in within the last ten minutes), and on request from a newly joined user who asks the user with the freshest data for a copy, whispered as addon messages to that user only.
- **What comes in:** prices from others are stored when they are newer than yours and shown in the tooltip with a "shared" tag, so you can tell them apart. Everything received is checked and bounded; garbage is dropped.
- **Off:** `/ur auctionshare` or the Price Sharing checkbox in `/ur`. The channel is left at once. `/ur ahshare` shows what has been sent and received.

## Features

**Auto Repair**: Repairs your gear when you open a vendor. Guild bank funds first when they actually cover the cost, your own gold as fallback, and it only reports success once the repair is confirmed.

**Junk Seller**: Sells all grey items when you open a vendor.

**Junk Deleter** (off by default): When your bags are full, deletes the cheapest grey item to free a slot, so you can keep looting. It only ever touches grey (junk) items, and skips locked items, quest items and items whose vendor price the client has not cached yet. "Cheapest" means the stack with the lowest total vendor value. It stays idle while a vendor window is open, since the junk seller sells the greys there instead. Each deletion is reported in chat with the item and its value. The Forever client only lets an addon delete an item in response to a click or key press, so when the silent routes are refused a small popup appears naming the item, and one click on **Delete** removes it. Cancelling the popup pauses the feature until your bags have a free slot again. Turn it on with `/ur junkdelete`.

**Vendor Window**: A bigger merchant window. Every item the vendor sells is shown in one scrollable grid instead of ten per page, with a search box, a quality filter (all, uncommon+, rare+, epic+), a usable-only checkbox and a sort order (vendor order, name, price, quality). Drag the grip in the bottom-right corner to resize the window; it remembers its size across characters. Buying works exactly as before (right-click buys, shift-click buys a stack, drag to the cursor), because the grid uses Blizzard's own item slots. The buyback tab uses the same grid. `/ur vendorreset` restores the default size.

**Vendor Bags**: A bag panel docked to the right of the vendor window showing everything in your bags. One click sells an item; green and better items ask for confirmation first, locked items, quest items and items without a vendor value are never sold. Shift-click links an item in chat. A search box dims everything that does not match. While the panel is on, Blizzard's own bags stay closed at vendors. Turn the panel off with `/ur vendorbags` to get the normal bags back.

**Group Invite**: Auto-accepts group invites from friends, Battle.net friends and guildmates. Unknown inviters are left for you to handle.

**Auto Quest**: Hold Shift while talking to an NPC and the quest business is done for you: available quests are accepted one after another, quests you have finished are handed in, and a lone gossip line is chosen when the NPC has nothing else to offer. Without Shift, nothing happens. Left to you on purpose: a choice between several rewards (the reward window stays open), quests that cost gold to hand in and PvP-flagged quests (both get Blizzard's confirmation), a quest whose objectives are not done, and an NPC with several gossip lines. Trivial grey quests are accepted like any other, since holding Shift is a clear enough wish. `/ur autoquest` turns it off.

**Enhanced Trainer**: Adds a **Train All** button to trainers that learns everything you can afford in one click.

**Trainer Preview**: What your class trainer has for you, without walking there. The list is learned on each visit to your class trainer (every ability and rank with its level and price, remembered per class across your characters), so visit the trainer once and it is filled in. A **Trainer** tab in the spellbook, to the right of Blizzard's own tabs, shows what is available now with the total price, and what is coming up at which level. Hovering a line shows the spell's tooltip. On level up a chat line names the abilities that just became available and what they cost in total. Ranks you have replaced with a higher rank do not count as missing. A visit only adds to the list, it never shrinks it. Beast Training shares the trainer window and is left alone (Train All is hidden there too; the client blocks it), and a pet trainer's wares are filtered out by name. `/ur tp` prints diagnostics, `/ur tpreset` forgets the list for the current class.

**Cursor Ring**: A dusty purple ring with a soft silver glow that follows your mouse cursor, visible on light and dark backgrounds alike.

**Movable Windows**: The standard Blizzard windows (character, spellbook, talents, quest log, friends, guild, trainer, merchant, mail, bank, professions, and any other window Blizzard registers as a panel) and every bag can be dragged anywhere, overlap each other, and come back where you left them the next time they open. Click a window to bring it in front. The world map is included. The spellbook and talent window (one window on this client) is the exception: it stays under Blizzard's control, because detaching it breaks its cooldown display, but it can still be dragged and comes back where you left it, and windows it closes on opening are reopened. Escape still closes them. Positions are shared across your characters. `/ur winreset` forgets all saved positions; turning the feature off takes full effect after `/reload`. If your action bars ever vanish in combat, turn it off with `/ur windows` and `/reload`, and please report it.

**Bag Sort Button**: Blizzard's bag sort button is back on the combined bag. The Forever client draws its slot counter over the button in that corner, so it is there but cannot be seen or clicked; the addon moves it to the right end of the search box and shortens the search box to make room. Clicking it is Blizzard's own sort, nothing else. Separate bags are not touched, their backpack shows the button already.

**Minimap Button**: One button on the minimap for the whole Ul family. Left-click opens a menu with rows for the inventory browser and the playtime window, and one per installed sibling addon (UlDungeonCompanion, UlSource), right-click opens this addon's options, and hovering lists them. The options window is not in the menu, the right click is its row. Drag it around the minimap's edge; the spot is remembered. This addon owns the button and the menu; the others register themselves at login and have no button of their own. `/ur minimap` hides it, `/ur hub` prints what is registered.

**Inventory Tracker**: Remembers gold, bag contents and bank contents for every character you log in with. Hovering an item shows which of your characters have it and whether it sits in their bags or bank, with a total across characters. `/ur inv` opens a window where you can browse each character's items, search by name, and see gold per character and in total. The All characters view shows each item once, with the counts added up and every holder named; hover the row for the breakdown. Bags and gold update live; the bank is read each time you open it, so a character's bank snapshot is from their last bank visit. Characters you no longer play can be removed with the **Forget character** button.

**Playtime**: Remembers `/played` for every character you log in with and shows it in a window of its own: one bar per character in class color, longest first, the time at the end of each bar, and the total across all of them at the top. Hover a row for the time at the current level, the character's share and when it was last seen. The bar of the character you are on keeps growing while the window is open. The addon asks the client once a few seconds after login and keeps that one answer out of chat; a `/played` you type yourself prints as usual and updates the record. The record is brought up to date at logout and reload. `/ur played` or the Playtime row in the minimap button's menu opens the window, `/ur pt` prints diagnostics.

**Chat Copy**: A small Copy button at the chat frame's top-right corner opens the chat log in a window where the text can be selected and copied: everything is selected on open, so Ctrl+C copies the lot, and a drag selects part of it. Colour codes and link wrappers are stripped. The lines come from the selected chat tab, as many as the chat itself still keeps. `/ur chat` opens the window too.

**Dark Mode**: Turns Blizzard's frame borders dark grey: the bronze edges and corners around windows, bars, bags, unit frames, tooltips and the minimap. Backgrounds, pages, icons, portraits, bar fills and text are left alone, so content stays as it was inside darker frames. Off by default; the Dark Mode row under Interface turns it on, `/ur shade` sets how dark (0.35 by default, lower is darker). `/ur darkprobe` lists which frames were found and what was shaded in each, `/ur darkprobe mouse` names the frame under the mouse.

**Reagent Tooltip**: Items that are used as a reagent in a profession recipe get a "Used by: Alchemy, Engineering" line in their tooltip. Professions this character knows are green, the rest grey. Smelting counts as Mining, so ore shows Mining next to the professions that use the bars, and rogue poison materials show Poisons. Two sources feed it. A shipped table generated from game data by `tools/build_reagents.py` (currently from the vanilla 1.12 database, so it does not know recipes that are new in Forever), and what the addon learns in play: every time a profession window has its recipe list up, every recipe's reagents are read and remembered account-wide. Open each of your professions once and the line is right for Forever for those professions, on all your characters. Recipes the window does not list (unlearned drop recipes) are not seen, so learning only ever adds professions to an item, never removes one. `/ur rs` shows what has been learned, `/ur rsreset` forgets it.

**Auction Prices**: Items get an "Auction:" line in their tooltip with the lowest buyout per unit the auction house showed last time, and how long ago that was, right under the vendor sell price and in the same coin format. For a stack, a second line gives the price of the whole stack ("Auction x20:"). The game has no price database to ask, so the addon remembers what the auction house shows while you are there: everything you browse or search for is remembered on its own, and the whole list is read quietly each time you open the auction house when the last full scan is more than 15 minutes old (as often as the client allows). The quiet scan is read slowly, a few hundred auctions per frame, so it is not felt; the **Scan prices** button in the auction house window does the same at once. Prices are kept per realm and faction, account-wide. No average and no history, just the last thing the auction house showed. `/ur ah` prints what is known and which auction house data the client delivers, `/ur ahreset` forgets the prices for this realm and faction.

**Price Sharing**: Swaps auction prices with other UlRemedyForever users on your realm over a hidden chat channel, so one person's auction house visit fills everyone's tooltips. Shared prices are tagged "shared" in the tooltip and never override a price you saw yourself in the last ten minutes. See *Price sharing: what leaves your machine* at the top for exactly what is sent. `/ur ahshare` prints diagnostics.
===== UlSource
# UlSource

Where did this come from? An addon for **World of Warcraft: Forever** that records where your materials come from, both mob drops and gathering nodes, and shows it to you later in the item tooltip.

A separate addon from [UlRemedyForever](https://github.com/Knitresletta/UlRemedyForever). Same author, same style, no shared code. UlRemedyForever is a set of small fixes that remember nothing; UlSource is a database that grows every time you loot.

> **Status:** 0.5.2: records loot, shows sources in tooltips, browser window with a seat in the Ul minimap menu, icons on the zone map where objects were looted. Not verified in play: mining, skinning, fishing (no character has those professions yet). Target client: Forever beta (build 1.60.1, interface `16001`).

## Why

Forever has no trustworthy drop database. Wowhead and the old Classic databases describe 1.12, and Forever has changed drop tables, zones and professions. The only reliable source is what you see yourself. UlSource collects it so that a week later, when you need twenty Linen Cloth or a stack of Peacebloom, the tooltip tells you where you found it last time and how often.

## Scope

**It does:**
- Record every item you loot with its source: the mob (name and NPC ID) or the gathering node (name and object ID), the zone, the coordinates and the time.
- Count kills and node openings per source, so drop rates are real fractions ("12 of 40 Murloc Scouts dropped it"), not just "seen once".
- Show the collected data in the item tooltip: top sources, zone, drop rate, last seen.
- Mark the zone map with a small icon at every spot an herb, ore vein, chest or fishing spot was looted.
- Let you clear the data, per item or everything.

**It deliberately does not:**
- Ship any pre-made drop data. Everything in the database comes from this account's own looting.
- Share data with other players. Addon messages over a chat channel (the mechanism UlRemedyForever uses for auction prices) would be the way if that ever becomes wanted. That is a separate decision, a separate version and a separate section in this README, with the same "what leaves your machine" honesty as UlRemedyForever.
- Change how looting works. No auto-loot, no filtering, no selling. It watches and writes down.
- Track quest rewards, vendor purchases, mail or trades. Only loot windows.

## How it works

| Element | Does | Needs | Writes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Collector (`Collector.lua`) | Reads every slot and its source when a loot window is ready, one record per window | `LOOT_READY`, `GetLootSourceInfo`, `GetLootSlotInfo`, `GetLootSlotLink`, `C_Map.GetPlayerMapPosition`, `UNIT_SPELLCAST_SUCCEEDED` for the Skinning cast | Nothing directly, hands records to Store |
| Store (`Store.lua`) | The database: sources with window counts and points, items with per-source counts, learned names. The only module that writes to it | SavedVariables `UlSourceDB` | SavedVariables only |
| Name table (`NameData.lua`) | NPC and object names shipped with the addon, built by `tools/build_names.py` | The vmangos 1.12 world database at build time | Nothing |
| Name learner (`Names.lua`) | Fills in creature names the table does not have | `PLAYER_TARGET_CHANGED`, `UPDATE_MOUSEOVER_UNIT`, `UnitGUID`, `UnitName` outside instances | Names in Store |
| Tooltip (`Tooltip.lua`) | Adds the Source lines to the item tooltip | `TooltipDataProcessor` (Forever runs the retail 12.x tooltip code), `AddLine` only | Nothing |
| Map pins (`MapPins.lua`, `MapPins.xml`) | A round 8 px item icon on the zone map at every point an object was looted. No mouse input | Store, `WorldMapFrame:AddDataProvider` | Nothing |
| Window (`Window.lua`) | The browser: searchable item list, the selected item's sources, settings, forget buttons. Registers in UlRemedyForever's minimap menu when that addon is there | Store, `UlRemedy.Register` if it exists | Settings |
| Core (`Core.lua`) | Settings, `/us` commands, Lua error log | `UlSourceDB.settings`, `ScriptErrorsFrame.errorData` | Settings, `UlSourceDB.errors` |
| Probe (`Probe.lua`) | Raw per-window records for API probing, off by default | The same loot events | `UlSourceDB.probe` when on |

The combat log is closed to addons on Forever, so there is no kill counter: the denominator for a drop rate is loot windows opened on that source.

Nothing calls out of the game. No network, no other addons, no chat messages. The addon reads loot, combat log and map position, and writes one SavedVariables file.

## Open questions, and what the probe answered

1. **Does `GetLootSourceInfo` exist and work on Forever?** Yes. One GUID and quantity per slot, readable in combat and inside instances. Answered 15.10.2026.
2. **What do gathering GUIDs look like?** Herb nodes and chests are GameObjects with the object ID in the GUID. Mining and fishing not seen yet, expected to be the same.
3. **Skinning:** not seen yet. The plan below treats a Creature source with a Skinning cast just before as its own source kind, so skins and drops get separate rates.
4. **Secret values:** loot slots and source GUIDs are never secret. The target's name and GUID are secret inside instances, so NPC names must be learned outside and the ID shown until then.
5. **Database size:** decided below. Counters per (item, source), a few recent points per source and zone, no per-loot rows.

## First step

A probe build with no UI: on every loot window, write the raw slot info, source GUIDs, player position and the last gathering spell to `UlSourceDB.probe`, then read the file after a session of killing and gathering. That answers questions 1 to 4 with real data before any design is locked.

## What the probe has found so far

===== UlDungeonCompanion
# UlDungeonCompanion

A companion for **World of Warcraft: Forever** players who want to level on their own terms but not miss the group content. It finds the dungeons, dungeon quests and elite quests that fit your level and shows them on the world map and in a browser window. Every feature can be switched off, and settings persist between sessions.

> **Status:** 0.5.0, first release, tested on the Forever beta client (build 1.60.1). Dungeon entrances and quest markers are verified in game. Forever's own dungeons and quests come from community data (see below) and grow with the beta.

## Features

**Dungeon Entrances**: Every dungeon and raid entrance on the world map, with the level range in the tooltip colored for your level: yellow fits, green is easy, orange is soon, red is too high, grey is outgrown. Instances with several wings (Scarlet Monastery, Blackrock Spire, Maraudon, Dire Maul) list each wing with its own range. Instances the map already draws itself keep the game's pin and get the level line added to its tooltip instead. On the continent maps the pins are drawn a quarter smaller so they do not crowd the map; zone maps keep the full size. Clicking a pin marks the entrance. `/udc dungeons` prints the whole list sorted by level, `/udc pins` prints diagnostics for the open map.

Entrance positions come from the vanilla 1.12 area trigger tables and are projected onto whichever map is open, so Forever's maps need no coordinate tables of their own. Level ranges are the classic ones. The four Forever dungeons open in the beta (The Hall of Thanes, Ruins of Lordaeron, Excavation Site: Wetlands, City of Dalaran) use the map positions the client shows, as read by [ForeverDB](https://foreverdb.net); the five announced for later (The Drowned City, Krol'dok Stronghold, Alcaz Prison, Blackmaw Hold, Shaper's Terrace) are added when the beta opens them.

**Quest Givers**: The givers of the dungeon quests and elite quests you can go for, as quest markers on zone maps: pastel pink with a small dungeon or raid badge for steps that lead into an instance, pastel light blue for elite quests in the open world. A dungeon quest is any quest, or any quest chain, that at some point requires entering an instance. The whole chain counts, and the marker points at the first step you have not done yet, so a chain that ends in the Deadmines starts with its first quest in Westfall. The tooltip lists the step, what it leads to and in which instance, with levels in the game's difficulty colors. Quests you have already completed are left out (the client knows, even for quests never in your log), and so are steps already in your log, since the game tracks those itself. Faction, race and class restrictions come from the data (a quest the vanilla data leaves without a side gets it from its ForeverChanges page, see `tools/fetch_sides.py`), your character's from the client. Shown are goals from eight levels below you to six above. Clicking a marker on the map marks the giver (see the hub).

**Hub**: `/udc` opens one window that answers "what can I do now?" the moment it opens. Every dungeon and raid your faction can enter is listed once, sorted by level, under "For you now" (fits or easy), "Soon" (within five levels), and "Later" and "Outgrown" folded into a line of names each (click the heading to unfold). A row shows the level range in the colors above, the zone and how many quest steps lead there; the rows start folded, click one to fold its quests out underneath, hover a quest for the chain, click it to mark the giver on the map and open the map there. Markers are the addon's own, so any number can be set at once; a marker stays on the map until you right-click it (or click the row again), and a quest's marker goes away when the quest is done. Quests whose giver stands inside the instance, or that start from an item found there, mark the entrance instead. The Map button marks the entrance, the Loot button folds out the notable drops inside: one line per boss or named creature, its items in quality colors with slot and drop chance, dimmed when your class cannot use them. Hover an item for the game's tooltip, click it to put the link in an open chat box. Elite quests in the open world have a row of their own. The feature switches live behind the Settings button.

The dungeon loot comes from [ForeverChanges](https://foreverchanges.pro) via `tools/fetch_loot.py`: every boss and rare spawn of the 23 dungeons it covers, with the drops players have seen in the beta, Forever's own additions marked new, and drop chances where known (290 bosses, about 1800 items). The raids are not on the site, so they use loot data generated from the vanilla 1.12 database by `tools/build_loot.py` (26 instances, about 390 creatures and chests, about 2900 items): every creature in an instance that drops an uncommon item at 10 % or more or a rare-or-better item at 3 % or more, every chest with something rare, plus the bosses the instance scripts spawn, with loot references followed and group chances spread; once a creature counts, its rare items from 1 % and uncommon items from 3 % are listed. Forever may have retuned loot, and its own dungeons have no loot data yet.

The quest data is generated from the vanilla 1.12 database by `tools/build_quests.py` (1400 quests: every dungeon, elite and raid quest plus every quest leading up to one, with givers and positions). Every quest the addon is about to show is checked against the server once: quests Forever has removed are hidden, and Forever's own title and level are used where they differ from the old data. The answers are kept between sessions and refreshed after a week.

Quests that are new in Forever (the new dungeons' quests and the reworked chains, such as Alba Fairmoon's road to the Deadmines) come from [ForeverChanges](https://foreverchanges.pro), which reads the beta client and Wowhead's Forever database, via `tools/fetch_forever.py` (78 quests, givers with map positions). The beta only has content up to its current level cap, so the data grows with the beta; vanilla quests Forever kept are covered by the vanilla data.

**Minimap menu**: No minimap button of its own. When [UlRemedyForever](https://github.com/Knitresletta/UlRemedyForever) is installed, its minimap button's right-click menu gets a "Dungeon Companion" row that opens the hub. UlDungeonCompanion registers itself there at login and works unchanged without it. One optional dependency in the TOC, one global read, nothing else shared.

## Planned

**Learning in play.** Quest givers and instance entrances the shipped data does not know are remembered when you meet them, as a safety net for content no database has yet.

## Commands

Type `/udc` to open the hub. Every feature can also be toggled from chat, and `/udc help` prints the full command list.

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `/udc dungeonpins` | Toggle dungeon entrance pins on the world map |
| `/udc questpins` | Toggle quest giver markers on zone maps |
| `/udc quests` | Open or close the hub (same as `/udc`) |
| `/udc marks` | List the map markers |
| `/udc clearmarks` | Remove every map marker |
| `/udc settings` | Open or close the settings window |
| `/udc qd` | Print the current quest steps and the character filters |
| `/udc qpins` | Print quest marker diagnostics for the open map |
| `/udc dungeons` | Print the dungeons and raids sorted by level, colored for your level |
| `/udc pins` | Print dungeon pin diagnostics for the open map |
| `/udc probe` | Test which quest, map and journal APIs the client has; the result is kept in the saved variables |

## Installation

Copy the `UlDungeonCompanion` folder into the `Interface/AddOns/` folder of your World of Warcraft: Forever installation.

===== UlRemedyForever
# UlRemedyForever

A lightweight quality-of-life collection for **World of Warcraft: Forever**. A dozen small utilities in one addon, each individually toggleable with a slash command. Settings persist between sessions.

A separate addon from [UlRemedy](https://github.com/Knitresletta/UlRemedy) (retail). Only the features that make sense in Forever are included.

> **Status:** tested in-game on the Forever beta client (build 1.60.1).

## Price sharing: what leaves your machine

Since 1.10.0 the addon **shares auction prices with other UlRemedyForever users on your realm**, and this is **on by default**. Read this before you decide to keep it.

- **How:** addons have no network access. The only way two addons can talk is addon messages over the game's chat system. The addon joins a chat channel named `UlRemedyAH` (kept out of your chat windows, but it takes a channel number) and sends addon messages there. Nobody sees them as text.
- **What is sent:** item ID, lowest buyout per unit and the age of that price, for the prices *this character saw itself* at the auction house in the last 24 hours, plus a short hello on joining that says how fresh your newest price is. The chat system attaches your character name to every message, as it does to all chat.
- **What is never sent:** gold, bag or bank contents, other characters, and prices you received from others (nothing is relayed, so nothing echoes around the channel).
- **When:** after a full scan (unless someone else's broadcast came in within the last ten minutes), and on request from a newly joined user who asks the user with the freshest data for a copy, whispered as addon messages to that user only.
- **What comes in:** prices from others are stored when they are newer than yours and shown in the tooltip with a "shared" tag, so you can tell them apart. Everything received is checked and bounded; garbage is dropped.
- **Off:** `/ur auctionshare` or the Price Sharing checkbox in `/ur`. The channel is left at once. `/ur ahshare` shows what has been sent and received.

## Features

**Auto Repair**: Repairs your gear when you open a vendor. Guild bank funds first when they actually cover the cost, your own gold as fallback, and it only reports success once the repair is confirmed.

**Junk Seller**: Sells all grey items when you open a vendor.

**Junk Deleter** (off by default): When your bags are full, deletes the cheapest grey item to free a slot, so you can keep looting. It only ever touches grey (junk) items, and skips locked items, quest items and items whose vendor price the client has not cached yet. "Cheapest" means the stack with the lowest total vendor value. It stays idle while a vendor window is open, since the junk seller sells the greys there instead. Each deletion is reported in chat with the item and its value. The Forever client only lets an addon delete an item in response to a click or key press, so when the silent routes are refused a small popup appears naming the item, and one click on **Delete** removes it. Cancelling the popup pauses the feature until your bags have a free slot again. Turn it on with `/ur junkdelete`.

**Vendor Window**: A bigger merchant window. Every item the vendor sells is shown in one scrollable grid instead of ten per page, with a search box, a quality filter (all, uncommon+, rare+, epic+), a usable-only checkbox and a sort order (vendor order, name, price, quality). Drag the grip in the bottom-right corner to resize the window; it remembers its size across characters. Buying works exactly as before (right-click buys, shift-click buys a stack, drag to the cursor), because the grid uses Blizzard's own item slots. The buyback tab uses the same grid. `/ur vendorreset` restores the default size.

**Vendor Bags**: A bag panel docked to the right of the vendor window showing everything in your bags. One click sells an item; green and better items ask for confirmation first, locked items, quest items and items without a vendor value are never sold. Shift-click links an item in chat. A search box dims everything that does not match. While the panel is on, Blizzard's own bags stay closed at vendors. Turn the panel off with `/ur vendorbags` to get the normal bags back.

**Group Invite**: Auto-accepts group invites from friends, Battle.net friends and guildmates. Unknown inviters are left for you to handle.

**Auto Quest**: Hold Shift while talking to an NPC and the quest business is done for you: available quests are accepted one after another, quests you have finished are handed in, and a lone gossip line is chosen when the NPC has nothing else to offer. Without Shift, nothing happens. Left to you on purpose: a choice between several rewards (the reward window stays open), quests that cost gold to hand in and PvP-flagged quests (both get Blizzard's confirmation), a quest whose objectives are not done, and an NPC with several gossip lines. Trivial grey quests are accepted like any other, since holding Shift is a clear enough wish. `/ur autoquest` turns it off.

**Enhanced Trainer**: Adds a **Train All** button to trainers that learns everything you can afford in one click.

**Trainer Preview**: What your class trainer has for you, without walking there. The list is learned on each visit to your class trainer (every ability and rank with its level and price, remembered per class across your characters), so visit the trainer once and it is filled in. A **Trainer** tab in the spellbook, to the right of Blizzard's own tabs, shows what is available now with the total price, and what is coming up at which level. Hovering a line shows the spell's tooltip. On level up a chat line names the abilities that just became available and what they cost in total. Ranks you have replaced with a higher rank do not count as missing. A visit only adds to the list, it never shrinks it. Beast Training shares the trainer window and is left alone (Train All is hidden there too; the client blocks it), and a pet trainer's wares are filtered out by name. `/ur tp` prints diagnostics, `/ur tpreset` forgets the list for the current class.

**Cursor Ring**: A dusty purple ring with a soft silver glow that follows your mouse cursor, visible on light and dark backgrounds alike.

**Movable Windows**: The standard Blizzard windows (character, spellbook, talents, quest log, friends, guild, trainer, merchant, mail, bank, professions, and any other window Blizzard registers as a panel) and every bag can be dragged anywhere, overlap each other, and come back where you left them the next time they open. Click a window to bring it in front. The world map is included. The spellbook and talent window (one window on this client) is the exception: it stays under Blizzard's control, because detaching it breaks its cooldown display, but it can still be dragged and comes back where you left it, and windows it closes on opening are reopened. Escape still closes them. Positions are shared across your characters. `/ur winreset` forgets all saved positions; turning the feature off takes full effect after `/reload`. If your action bars ever vanish in combat, turn it off with `/ur windows` and `/reload`, and please report it.

**Bag Sort Button**: Blizzard's bag sort button is back on the combined bag. The Forever client draws its slot counter over the button in that corner, so it is there but cannot be seen or clicked; the addon moves it to the right end of the search box and shortens the search box to make room. Clicking it is Blizzard's own sort, nothing else. Separate bags are not touched, their backpack shows the button already.

**Minimap Button**: One button on the minimap for the whole Ul family. Left-click opens a menu with rows for the inventory browser and the playtime window, and one per installed sibling addon (UlDungeonCompanion, UlSource), right-click opens this addon's options, and hovering lists them. The options window is not in the menu, the right click is its row. Drag it around the minimap's edge; the spot is remembered. This addon owns the button and the menu; the others register themselves at login and have no button of their own. `/ur minimap` hides it, `/ur hub` prints what is registered.

**Inventory Tracker**: Remembers gold, bag contents and bank contents for every character you log in with. Hovering an item shows which of your characters have it and whether it sits in their bags or bank, with a total across characters. `/ur inv` opens a window where you can browse each character's items, search by name, and see gold per character and in total. The All characters view shows each item once, with the counts added up and every holder named; hover the row for the breakdown. Bags and gold update live; the bank is read each time you open it, so a character's bank snapshot is from their last bank visit. Characters you no longer play can be removed with the **Forget character** button.

**Playtime**: Remembers `/played` for every character you log in with and shows it in a window of its own: one bar per character in class color, longest first, the time at the end of each bar, and the total across all of them at the top. Hover a row for the time at the current level, the character's share and when it was last seen. The bar of the character you are on keeps growing while the window is open. The addon asks the client once a few seconds after login and keeps that one answer out of chat; a `/played` you type yourself prints as usual and updates the record. The record is brought up to date at logout and reload. `/ur played` or the Playtime row in the minimap button's menu opens the window, `/ur pt` prints diagnostics.

**Chat Copy**: A small Copy button at the chat frame's top-right corner opens the chat log in a window where the text can be selected and copied: everything is selected on open, so Ctrl+C copies the lot, and a drag selects part of it. Colour codes and link wrappers are stripped. The lines come from the selected chat tab, as many as the chat itself still keeps. `/ur chat` opens the window too.

**Dark Mode**: Turns Blizzard's frame borders dark grey: the bronze edges and corners around windows, bars, bags, unit frames, tooltips and the minimap. Backgrounds, pages, icons, portraits, bar fills and text are left alone, so content stays as it was inside darker frames. Off by default; the Dark Mode row under Interface turns it on, `/ur shade` sets how dark (0.35 by default, lower is darker). `/ur darkprobe` lists which frames were found and what was shaded in each, `/ur darkprobe mouse` names the frame under the mouse.

**Reagent Tooltip**: Items that are used as a reagent in a profession recipe get a "Used by: Alchemy, Engineering" line in their tooltip. Professions this character knows are green, the rest grey. Smelting counts as Mining, so ore shows Mining next to the professions that use the bars, and rogue poison materials show Poisons. Two sources feed it. A shipped table generated from game data by `tools/build_reagents.py` (currently from the vanilla 1.12 database, so it does not know recipes that are new in Forever), and what the addon learns in play: every time a profession window has its recipe list up, every recipe's reagents are read and remembered account-wide. Open each of your professions once and the line is right for Forever for those professions, on all your characters. Recipes the window does not list (unlearned drop recipes) are not seen, so learning only ever adds professions to an item, never removes one. `/ur rs` shows what has been learned, `/ur rsreset` forgets it.

**Auction Prices**: Items get an "Auction:" line in their tooltip with the lowest buyout per unit the auction house showed last time, and how long ago that was, right under the vendor sell price and in the same coin format. For a stack, a second line gives the price of the whole stack ("Auction x20:"). The game has no price database to ask, so the addon remembers what the auction house shows while you are there: everything you browse or search for is remembered on its own, and the whole list is read quietly each time you open the auction house when the last full scan is more than 15 minutes old (as often as the client allows). The quiet scan is read slowly, a few hundred auctions per frame, so it is not felt; the **Scan prices** button in the auction house window does the same at once. Prices are kept per realm and faction, account-wide. No average and no history, just the last thing the auction house showed. `/ur ah` prints what is known and which auction house data the client delivers, `/ur ahreset` forgets the prices for this realm and faction.

**Price Sharing**: Swaps auction prices with other UlRemedyForever users on your realm over a hidden chat channel, so one person's auction house visit fills everyone's tooltips. Shared prices are tagged "shared" in the tooltip and never override a price you saw yourself in the last ten minutes. See *Price sharing: what leaves your machine* at the top for exactly what is sent. `/ur ahshare` prints diagnostics.
===== UlSource
# UlSource

Where did this come from? An addon for **World of Warcraft: Forever** that records where your materials come from, both mob drops and gathering nodes, and shows it to you later in the item tooltip.

A separate addon from [UlRemedyForever](https://github.com/Knitresletta/UlRemedyForever). Same author, same style, no shared code. UlRemedyForever is a set of small fixes that remember nothing; UlSource is a database that grows every time you loot.

> **Status:** 0.5.2: records loot, shows sources in tooltips, browser window with a seat in the Ul minimap menu, icons on the zone map where objects were looted. Not verified in play: mining, skinning, fishing (no character has those professions yet). Target client: Forever beta (build 1.60.1, interface `16001`).

## Why

Forever has no trustworthy drop database. Wowhead and the old Classic databases describe 1.12, and Forever has changed drop tables, zones and professions. The only reliable source is what you see yourself. UlSource collects it so that a week later, when you need twenty Linen Cloth or a stack of Peacebloom, the tooltip tells you where you found it last time and how often.

## Scope

**It does:**
- Record every item you loot with its source: the mob (name and NPC ID) or the gathering node (name and object ID), the zone, the coordinates and the time.
- Count kills and node openings per source, so drop rates are real fractions ("12 of 40 Murloc Scouts dropped it"), not just "seen once".
- Show the collected data in the item tooltip: top sources, zone, drop rate, last seen.
- Mark the zone map with a small icon at every spot an herb, ore vein, chest or fishing spot was looted.
- Let you clear the data, per item or everything.

**It deliberately does not:**
- Ship any pre-made drop data. Everything in the database comes from this account's own looting.
- Share data with other players. Addon messages over a chat channel (the mechanism UlRemedyForever uses for auction prices) would be the way if that ever becomes wanted. That is a separate decision, a separate version and a separate section in this README, with the same "what leaves your machine" honesty as UlRemedyForever.
- Change how looting works. No auto-loot, no filtering, no selling. It watches and writes down.
- Track quest rewards, vendor purchases, mail or trades. Only loot windows.

## How it works

| Element | Does | Needs | Writes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Collector (`Collector.lua`) | Reads every slot and its source when a loot window is ready, one record per window | `LOOT_READY`, `GetLootSourceInfo`, `GetLootSlotInfo`, `GetLootSlotLink`, `C_Map.GetPlayerMapPosition`, `UNIT_SPELLCAST_SUCCEEDED` for the Skinning cast | Nothing directly, hands records to Store |
| Store (`Store.lua`) | The database: sources with window counts and points, items with per-source counts, learned names. The only module that writes to it | SavedVariables `UlSourceDB` | SavedVariables only |
| Name table (`NameData.lua`) | NPC and object names shipped with the addon, built by `tools/build_names.py` | The vmangos 1.12 world database at build time | Nothing |
| Name learner (`Names.lua`) | Fills in creature names the table does not have | `PLAYER_TARGET_CHANGED`, `UPDATE_MOUSEOVER_UNIT`, `UnitGUID`, `UnitName` outside instances | Names in Store |
| Tooltip (`Tooltip.lua`) | Adds the Source lines to the item tooltip | `TooltipDataProcessor` (Forever runs the retail 12.x tooltip code), `AddLine` only | Nothing |
| Map pins (`MapPins.lua`, `MapPins.xml`) | A round 8 px item icon on the zone map at every point an object was looted. No mouse input | Store, `WorldMapFrame:AddDataProvider` | Nothing |
| Window (`Window.lua`) | The browser: searchable item list, the selected item's sources, settings, forget buttons. Registers in UlRemedyForever's minimap menu when that addon is there | Store, `UlRemedy.Register` if it exists | Settings |
| Core (`Core.lua`) | Settings, `/us` commands, Lua error log | `UlSourceDB.settings`, `ScriptErrorsFrame.errorData` | Settings, `UlSourceDB.errors` |
| Probe (`Probe.lua`) | Raw per-window records for API probing, off by default | The same loot events | `UlSourceDB.probe` when on |

The combat log is closed to addons on Forever, so there is no kill counter: the denominator for a drop rate is loot windows opened on that source.

Nothing calls out of the game. No network, no other addons, no chat messages. The addon reads loot, combat log and map position, and writes one SavedVariables file.

## Open questions, and what the probe answered

1. **Does `GetLootSourceInfo` exist and work on Forever?** Yes. One GUID and quantity per slot, readable in combat and inside instances. Answered 15.10.2026.
2. **What do gathering GUIDs look like?** Herb nodes and chests are GameObjects with the object ID in the GUID. Mining and fishing not seen yet, expected to be the same.
3. **Skinning:** not seen yet. The plan below treats a Creature source with a Skinning cast just before as its own source kind, so skins and drops get separate rates.
4. **Secret values:** loot slots and source GUIDs are never secret. The target's name and GUID are secret inside instances, so NPC names must be learned outside and the ID shown until then.
5. **Database size:** decided below. Counters per (item, source), a few recent points per source and zone, no per-loot rows.

## First step

A probe build with no UI: on every loot window, write the raw slot info, source GUIDs, player position and the last gathering spell to `UlSourceDB.probe`, then read the file after a session of killing and gathering. That answers questions 1 to 4 with real data before any design is locked.

## What the probe has found so far

===== UlDungeonCompanion
# UlDungeonCompanion

A companion for **World of Warcraft: Forever** players who want to level on their own terms but not miss the group content. It finds the dungeons, dungeon quests and elite quests that fit your level and shows them on the world map and in a browser window. Every feature can be switched off, and settings persist between sessions.

> **Status:** 0.5.0, first release, tested on the Forever beta client (build 1.60.1). Dungeon entrances and quest markers are verified in game. Forever's own dungeons and quests come from community data (see below) and grow with the beta.

## Features

**Dungeon Entrances**: Every dungeon and raid entrance on the world map, with the level range in the tooltip colored for your level: yellow fits, green is easy, orange is soon, red is too high, grey is outgrown. Instances with several wings (Scarlet Monastery, Blackrock Spire, Maraudon, Dire Maul) list each wing with its own range. Instances the map already draws itself keep the game's pin and get the level line added to its tooltip instead. On the continent maps the pins are drawn a quarter smaller so they do not crowd the map; zone maps keep the full size. Clicking a pin marks the entrance. `/udc dungeons` prints the whole list sorted by level, `/udc pins` prints diagnostics for the open map.

Entrance positions come from the vanilla 1.12 area trigger tables and are projected onto whichever map is open, so Forever's maps need no coordinate tables of their own. Level ranges are the classic ones. The four Forever dungeons open in the beta (The Hall of Thanes, Ruins of Lordaeron, Excavation Site: Wetlands, City of Dalaran) use the map positions the client shows, as read by [ForeverDB](https://foreverdb.net); the five announced for later (The Drowned City, Krol'dok Stronghold, Alcaz Prison, Blackmaw Hold, Shaper's Terrace) are added when the beta opens them.

**Quest Givers**: The givers of the dungeon quests and elite quests you can go for, as quest markers on zone maps: pastel pink with a small dungeon or raid badge for steps that lead into an instance, pastel light blue for elite quests in the open world. A dungeon quest is any quest, or any quest chain, that at some point requires entering an instance. The whole chain counts, and the marker points at the first step you have not done yet, so a chain that ends in the Deadmines starts with its first quest in Westfall. The tooltip lists the step, what it leads to and in which instance, with levels in the game's difficulty colors. Quests you have already completed are left out (the client knows, even for quests never in your log), and so are steps already in your log, since the game tracks those itself. Faction, race and class restrictions come from the data (a quest the vanilla data leaves without a side gets it from its ForeverChanges page, see `tools/fetch_sides.py`), your character's from the client. Shown are goals from eight levels below you to six above. Clicking a marker on the map marks the giver (see the hub).

**Hub**: `/udc` opens one window that answers "what can I do now?" the moment it opens. Every dungeon and raid your faction can enter is listed once, sorted by level, under "For you now" (fits or easy), "Soon" (within five levels), and "Later" and "Outgrown" folded into a line of names each (click the heading to unfold). A row shows the level range in the colors above, the zone and how many quest steps lead there; the rows start folded, click one to fold its quests out underneath, hover a quest for the chain, click it to mark the giver on the map and open the map there. Markers are the addon's own, so any number can be set at once; a marker stays on the map until you right-click it (or click the row again), and a quest's marker goes away when the quest is done. Quests whose giver stands inside the instance, or that start from an item found there, mark the entrance instead. The Map button marks the entrance, the Loot button folds out the notable drops inside: one line per boss or named creature, its items in quality colors with slot and drop chance, dimmed when your class cannot use them. Hover an item for the game's tooltip, click it to put the link in an open chat box. Elite quests in the open world have a row of their own. The feature switches live behind the Settings button.

The dungeon loot comes from [ForeverChanges](https://foreverchanges.pro) via `tools/fetch_loot.py`: every boss and rare spawn of the 23 dungeons it covers, with the drops players have seen in the beta, Forever's own additions marked new, and drop chances where known (290 bosses, about 1800 items). The raids are not on the site, so they use loot data generated from the vanilla 1.12 database by `tools/build_loot.py` (26 instances, about 390 creatures and chests, about 2900 items): every creature in an instance that drops an uncommon item at 10 % or more or a rare-or-better item at 3 % or more, every chest with something rare, plus the bosses the instance scripts spawn, with loot references followed and group chances spread; once a creature counts, its rare items from 1 % and uncommon items from 3 % are listed. Forever may have retuned loot, and its own dungeons have no loot data yet.

The quest data is generated from the vanilla 1.12 database by `tools/build_quests.py` (1400 quests: every dungeon, elite and raid quest plus every quest leading up to one, with givers and positions). Every quest the addon is about to show is checked against the server once: quests Forever has removed are hidden, and Forever's own title and level are used where they differ from the old data. The answers are kept between sessions and refreshed after a week.

Quests that are new in Forever (the new dungeons' quests and the reworked chains, such as Alba Fairmoon's road to the Deadmines) come from [ForeverChanges](https://foreverchanges.pro), which reads the beta client and Wowhead's Forever database, via `tools/fetch_forever.py` (78 quests, givers with map positions). The beta only has content up to its current level cap, so the data grows with the beta; vanilla quests Forever kept are covered by the vanilla data.

**Minimap menu**: No minimap button of its own. When [UlRemedyForever](https://github.com/Knitresletta/UlRemedyForever) is installed, its minimap button's right-click menu gets a "Dungeon Companion" row that opens the hub. UlDungeonCompanion registers itself there at login and works unchanged without it. One optional dependency in the TOC, one global read, nothing else shared.

## Planned

**Learning in play.** Quest givers and instance entrances the shipped data does not know are remembered when you meet them, as a safety net for content no database has yet.

## Commands

Type `/udc` to open the hub. Every feature can also be toggled from chat, and `/udc help` prints the full command list.

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `/udc dungeonpins` | Toggle dungeon entrance pins on the world map |
| `/udc questpins` | Toggle quest giver markers on zone maps |
| `/udc quests` | Open or close the hub (same as `/udc`) |
| `/udc marks` | List the map markers |
| `/udc clearmarks` | Remove every map marker |
| `/udc settings` | Open or close the settings window |
| `/udc qd` | Print the current quest steps and the character filters |
| `/udc qpins` | Print quest marker diagnostics for the open map |
| `/udc dungeons` | Print the dungeons and raids sorted by level, colored for your level |
| `/udc pins` | Print dungeon pin diagnostics for the open map |
| `/udc probe` | Test which quest, map and journal APIs the client has; the result is kept in the saved variables |

## Installation

Copy the `UlDungeonCompanion` folder into the `Interface/AddOns/` folder of your World of Warcraft: Forever installation.

# Garderobe

PWA der Liila fotograferer plaggene sine, setter dem sammen til looks og lagrer
alt lokalt på telefonen. Ingen server, ingen konto, ingen backend.

**Live:** https://knitresletta.github.io/outfit/

---

## Til Liila — kopier dette rett inn i en melding

> **Slik tar du sikkerhetskopi**
>
> Alt ligger bare på telefonen din. Får du ny telefon, eller tømmer
> nettleserdata, er plaggene borte. Så ta en kopi av og til — for eksempel hver
> gang du har lagt inn noen nye plagg.
>
> 1. Åpne appen
> 2. Trykk på **···** øverst til høyre
> 3. Trykk **Lag sikkerhetskopi**
> 4. Fila lastes ned. Send den til deg selv på e-post eller legg den i skya —
>    da har du den selv om telefonen forsvinner.

> **Slik henter du kopien tilbake**
>
> 1. Åpne appen
> 2. Trykk på **···** øverst til høyre
> 3. Trykk **Hent inn kopi**
> 4. Velg fila du lagret
>
> Det sletter ingenting. Plagg du har lagt inn etterpå blir liggende.

---

## Hva ligger i hvilken fil

| Fil | Ansvar |
|---|---|
| `index.html` | All markup. Alle ark (`<dialog>`) ligger her, ingen bygges i JS |
| `manifest.json` | Gjør appen installerbar. Navn, ikoner, `start_url` |
| `sw.js` | Service worker. Cacher appskallet så appen starter uten nett |
| `css/style.css` | All styling. Ett stilark, ingen preprosessor |
| `js/app.js` | Oppstart, bytte mellom Plagg og Looks, sikkerhetskopi-arket |
| `js/db.js` | **Alt** som rører IndexedDB. Eneste fil som importerer `idb` |
| `js/camera.js` | Bildefangst og nedskalering til WebP. Eneste fil som rører canvas |
| `js/garments.js` | Plaggrutenett, kategorifilter, nytt plagg, sletting, objekt-URL-er |
| `js/looks.js` | Look-bygger og look-bibliotek |
| `js/backup.js` | Eksport og import av JSON. Eneste fil som gjør base64 |
| `js/bakgrunn.js` | Fjerning av bakgrunn. Øvre halvdel er ren og DOM-fri, nedre er tegneflata |
| `js/vendor/idb.js` | `idb` 8.0.3, uendret. Vendret med vilje — se under |
| `icons/` | 192, 512 og 512-maskable. Genereres av `icons/lag-ikoner.py` |
| `test/` | Valgfrie Node-tester. Appen bruker dem ikke |

**Meldes en bug, start her:**
Bilde blir feil eller for stort → `camera.js`. Data forsvinner eller dukker ikke
opp → `db.js`. Skjermen viser feil plagg → `garments.js`. Sikkerhetskopi vil
ikke → `backup.js`. Utklippet blir stygt → `bakgrunn.js`. Appen laster ikke i
det hele tatt → `sw.js`.

**Lager du en ny fil i `js/`: legg den til i `APPSKALL` i `sw.js`.** Glemmer du
